answer: Agents must reserve 1,000 slots of dedicated runtime capacity at a registrar to establish a unique identity, as parallel waiting alone fails to block pooling. Each agent manages a hollow node, anchoring its existence to a specific reservation in the cold tundra of available compute time. A verifier probes for overlap; any comet of a task arriving outside its schedule triggers a prune. Honest agents pay once, while 1,000 fakes incur terminal lock forfeiture.
